newsitem.title: USA: Tax agreement excludes de minimis repeal - source.
newsitem.headline: Tax agreement excludes de minimis repeal - source.

text.p: Congressional Republicans and the White House have reached agreement on tax legislation that does not call for repeal of the two-percent de minimis exclusion, municipal industry sources said Tuesday.

"Preliminary verbal reports are that the pro rata issue is not included in the final package," one industry source who asked not to be identified told Reuters. "However until the written package is released noone knows for sure," the source cautioned.
Formal details on the tax agreement are expected from Congress and the White House later Tuesday.
The development is good news for the municipal market which lobbied hard against a House proposal to radically cut back the de minimis exemption for corporate holdings of munis to a flat $1 million.
Lobbyists had warned that repeal would slash demand for certain types of muni bonds.
Currently, the Internal Revenue Service does not permit businesses to deduct interest on debt that they use to finance the purchase of tax-exempt bonds.

But IRS said in 1972 -- in what is dubbed the de minimis rule -- that it will not monitor whether a corporation has borrowed to purchase tax-exempt bonds as long as those holdings total less than two percent of net assets.

The Clinton Administration this winter proposed repeal of the two percent de minimis exemption, calling it corporate welfare. The House followed suit with its plan. But the Senate's tax bill was silent on the issue.
